input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling (customer) an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit cost — 90 days' notice sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60–90 days) and the absence of any termination fee is better than the fallback cap of three months' fees. Garman has no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling on notice under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency/uncured material default under 17(c), and Section 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term without any Garman right to walk away or suspend at will. Section 17(a) also keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in. Noted but not flagged as a deviation: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund in 17(c)/p0128 applies only on Garman default), which is a sub-element short of the preferred position rather than a failure of the fallback, and fee exposure is limited given the annual maintenance term.
